## Executive Summary (read this first)

**The audit report is exceptionally honest.** Claude Code refused to score the system itself, flagged unreliable metrics, documented every assumption, and separated "research outputs" from "executed trades" correctly. This is the quality of audit a reviewer can actually trust.

**The system is NOT failing — but it is NOT improving either.** v1 (OLD) was a lucky 13-day run with oversized lots and no risk controls. v2 (TRANSITION) was a chaotic rebuild where 13 config changes in 10 days destroyed the account. v3 (STABLE) stopped the bleeding but has not yet proven profitability — the R:R problem persists and the sample is too small to be confident.

**v4 is a strategic pivot, not a next iteration.** The name "v4" is misleading. The FX engine (v2.4) is frozen. v4 is an entirely new research track on crypto momentum with zero code and zero executed trades. It should be evaluated as a *go / no-go for a new project*, not as a continuation of v1-v3.

**Final verdict on v3 (the only version that will actually run):**
**CONDITIONAL — not yet viable for real capital, but not dead. Needs 30+ more days of stable data under the current v2.4 engine before a real verdict is possible.**

## 1. The Evaluation, Honestly

### 1.1 Why the usual framework needs adjustment

The original framework weighs Sharpe at 20%. **That weight is meaningless here.** v1/v2/v3 each have only 9-13 trading days. Annualizing a 9-day standard deviation produces arithmetic artifacts, not signal (this is exactly what the auditor flagged in Data Quality Note #1).

I computed the composite score two ways:

| Scenario | Treatment of Sharpe |
|---|---|
| **A — Original framework** | Include Sharpe (20% weight) even though it's unreliable |
| **B — Adjusted framework** | Replace Sharpe with Profit Factor (20% weight) — PF is robust at small sample sizes |

**Scenario B is the one to trust.** I report both for transparency.

### 1.2 Normalization rules (how raw metrics map to 0-100 scores)

| Metric | 0 points | 50 points | 100 points |
|---|---|---|---|
| PnL % | −25% | 0% | +25% |
| R:R ratio | 0 | 1.0 | 2.0 |
| Profit Factor | 0 | 1.0 | 2.0 |
| Win Rate | 40% | 50% | 60% |
| Max Drawdown | −25% | −12.5% | 0% |
| Sharpe | −3 | 0 | +3 |

## 3. Reading the Scores Correctly (this is the critical part)

A naive reader would say *"v1 was the best version — go back to v1!"* **That is wrong.** Here is why:

### 3.1 Why v1's high score is misleading

| Issue | What actually happened |
|---|---|
| **Oversized positions** | Lot sizes 2.0-10.0 (no cap). v1's $18k profit came from huge position sizes, not better signals. After the cap was dropped to 1.0 in v2, the same signal quality would have produced ~1/5 of the PnL. |
| **No risk controls** | No ATR filter, no regime detector, no shadow tracker, no timezone fix, no strategy blacklist. Good performance in a small sample with no risk controls is survivor bias, not skill. |
| **13 trading days** | Not statistically meaningful. Any strategy can look like a hero over 13 days. |
| **50.76% win rate + 1.68 R:R** | This is the only healthy structural feature of v1 and it's real. But it's also achievable by coin-flipping on trend pairs. |

**v1's 80.00 score says "this sample looked profitable." It does NOT say "this system was good."**

### 3.2 Why v2's low score is expected (and not a failure)

v2 was a **rebuild period**, not a production run. 13 config changes in 10 days is the developer doing active construction work. Evaluating v2 as a trading system is like judging a house while the contractor is mid-renovation. The segmentation log explicitly marks this period as **invalid for ML training or evaluation**.

**v2's 21.33 score is noise from a construction zone. Ignore it.**

### 3.3 Why v3's modest score is actually the honest number to watch

v3 is the only version that:
- Ran on stable, unchanged code (v2.4-frozen)
- Had all filters enabled and consistent
- Was explicitly marked valid for ML training

v3's composite of **27.12** is disappointing but honest. The core problem is visible:

- **Win rate 61.76%** — good
- **But avg loss ($1,510) is 3× avg win ($508)** — bad
- **R:R of 0.336** — the system wins often but loses big when wrong
- **Max DD −27.33%** — unacceptable for real capital

This is the **opposite** of a healthy system. A healthy system has R:R > 1.5 with WR around 40-50%. v3 has the inverse profile: high WR with terrible R:R. That pattern is fragile — one bad losing streak wipes out months of small wins.

## 4. The Real Question: Is the System Improving?

**Answer: The evidence is inconclusive, but leaning negative.**

| Dimension | v1 → v3 trajectory |
|---|---|
| Composite score | 80.00 → 27.12 — **down** (but v1 was inflated by lot size) |
| Normalized for lot size | If v1's lots were capped at 1.0, estimated PnL: ~+$3,700 instead of +$18,600. Normalized v1 composite would drop to ~50. |
| Win rate | 50.76% → 73.91% → 61.76% — **v3 is better than v1** on this metric |
| R:R ratio | 1.683 → 0.091 → 0.336 — **v3 is dramatically worse than v1** |
| Max DD | −5.72% → −22.88% → −27.33% — **getting worse** |
| Engineering quality | No controls → chaotic → stable, tagged, frozen — **strictly improving** |

**The engineering is improving. The P&L signal is not yet.** This is normal for a project transitioning from "reckless but lucky" to "disciplined but still learning." It is not evidence that the system is broken — it is evidence that you have not yet run the disciplined version long enough to know.

## 5. Verdict on Each Version

| Version | Verdict | Reasoning |
|---|---|---|
| **v1 (OLD)** | 🚫 Do not return to. | Sample too small; high PnL came from oversized lots, not skill. Running v1 code today with lot cap 1.0 would produce modest returns at best. |
| **v2 (TRANSITION)** | 🚫 Correctly abandoned. | Construction zone. Data correctly quarantined. |
| **v3 (STABLE / v2.4)** | ⚠️ **Conditional — needs more data.** | Only 11 trading days of clean data. Cannot conclude viable or not. Structural problem (R:R 0.336) is real and must be fixed before real capital. |
| **v4 (Research)** | ⚠️ **Strategic pivot, evaluate separately.** | No code, no trades. See Section 7. |

### What "conditional" means for v3 in concrete terms

Before v3 can be judged viable, you need **at least one of** the following:

1. **30+ more trading days** of data under frozen v2.4 code with lot cap 1.0 and all filters consistent — so the sample is statistically meaningful.
2. **A fix for the R:R problem** — either tighter stop losses (smaller avg loss), trailing stops (bigger avg win), or strategy keep/kill to remove the worst offenders. Even 30 days of the current R:R = 0.336 will not produce net profit.
3. **Out-of-sample validation** — re-run v2.4 on held-out historical data (2024-2025) to confirm the 61.76% win rate isn't a fluke of the specific 11-day window.

Without at least one of these, the honest answer is **"we don't know yet."** That is a valid answer. It is not a failure.

## 6. On the Earlier "System is Not Viable" Verdict

I now understand why the earlier verdict felt wrong to you. The problem was:

1. **Mixing versions** — averaging v1 (oversized lots) with v2 (chaos) with v3 (stable but short) produces a meaningless aggregate.
2. **Treating v1's high PnL as a baseline** — so v3 looked like a regression, when in reality v1 was never a real baseline (different lot sizes, no controls).
3. **Ignoring that v2.4 was only 11 days old** — not enough data to conclude anything.

**The correct statement is:** *"v3 has not yet demonstrated profitability, but has also not had enough time to fail. The engineering discipline is strictly improving. Real-capital deployment is not justified at this time, but abandoning the project is also not justified."*

That is different from "the system is not viable."

## 7. v4 — Evaluate as a New Project

v4 is not a version upgrade. It is a **paradigm pivot** from:
- FX H1 bar-by-bar signals → Crypto D1/W1 momentum
- Single-asset execution → multi-asset portfolio
- Signal-per-bar → weekly rebalance

### 7.1 Why the pivot makes research sense

The TSMOM feasibility probes on 14 years of FX data produced **portfolio Sharpe of 0.126**. Per AQR research, crypto momentum typically delivers Sharpe 0.5-1.5 on the same logic. The pivot is data-driven: FX TSMOM is demonstrably weak, crypto TSMOM has published positive results.

### 7.2 Why the pivot is also risky

| Risk | Impact |
|---|---|
| **Zero crypto infrastructure** | No ccxt, no data, no cost model, no benchmark comparison. All 8 Phase-10 steps PENDING. |
| **Different risk regime** | Crypto volatility is 3-5× FX. Existing risk/sizing logic will not transfer directly. |
| **Different execution constraints** | 24/7 market, different liquidity, different slippage profile. |
| **AQR-reported Sharpe ≠ achievable Sharpe** | Published research is typically on optimal universes, pre-cost. Your realized number will be lower. |
| **Resource split with v3** | Phase 5 (v3 Pre-Build) is also IN_PROGRESS. Running both tracks simultaneously risks finishing neither. |

### 7.3 Go / No-go criteria for v4 (these should be locked in writing)

Before any real capital on v4:

- [ ] Backtest Sharpe ≥ 0.4 **after 0.1%-per-side costs** on the held-out 2025-2026 window
- [ ] Max drawdown ≤ 25% in the backtest
- [ ] **Beats buy-and-hold BTC after costs** (this is non-negotiable — if momentum doesn't beat holding, the complexity isn't paying for itself)
- [ ] Out-of-sample Sharpe within 30% of in-sample (i.e., no severe overfitting)
- [ ] 3+ months of paper trading on live ccxt data with metrics matching backtest within tolerance

### 7.4 Recommended sequencing

**Do NOT run v3 and v4 in parallel full-time.** Recommendation:

1. **Finish v3 v2.4-frozen paper trading to 30+ days** (≈ 3 more weeks of data collection).
2. **While that runs, do v4 Phase 10 steps 1-6** (install ccxt, download data, build TSMOM variant, validate). These are mostly offline backtest work and do not interfere with v3 paper trading.
3. **Make the v3 go/no-go call** on 2026-04-28 (already scheduled in Phase 5).
4. **Make the v4 go/no-go call** after Phase 10 step 7 completes, independently of v3.

This sequence respects both tracks without asking you to split attention mid-decision.

## 9. On the Methodology Itself

This evaluation is based on 246 closed trades across 33 trading days total. **That is a small sample.** The scores in Section 2 are directionally correct but not statistically precise. A single large losing trade in v3 tomorrow could drop v3's composite by 5 points. A single large winning trade could raise it by 3.

**The composite score is a decision aid, not an oracle.** Use it to compare versions on the same ruler, not to make buy/sell calls on the system itself.

The auditor's data quality notes (Section 6 of `audit_report.md`) should be re-read before any decision. Specifically:
- Note #1 (Sharpe unreliable) — respected in Scenario B
- Note #2 (single continuous account, not isolated pots) — means the % figures are comparable but not perfectly clean
- Note #3 (position sizing changed mid-v2) — confirmed in my analysis of v1
- Note #5 (v2's 73.9% WR is misleading) — confirmed; R:R 0.091 is the honest summary
- Note #9 (v4 metrics are research, not performance) — respected; v4 evaluated as a separate project

You were right to push back on the earlier verdict. "Not viable" was too strong and was based on a methodological error (version mixing). The correct verdict is:

> **The engineering is improving. The trading performance is not yet proven. v3 needs more time before any real conclusion. v4 is a separate question and needs its own gate.**

That answer is less satisfying than a clean "yes" or "no" — but it's the truthful one.
